Steph / Monica — first-pass findings below after checking the reserved pool metrics and scheduler logs for DL-2387 (PrimeLedger). Short summary: dedicated pool experienced both headroom exhaustion and increased queueing during the 22:30–23:15 window; autoscale did not add nodes fast enough due to an atypical spike pattern plus the pool hit a per-tenant cap for headroom.

What I looked at:
- GPU utilization: average 92% for the assigned worker set, occasional >98% on a subset of nodes.
- Queue lengths: token queue depth spiked ~3.8x baseline; average latency climbed with queueing + backpressure.
- Scheduler events: three scale-up attempts initiated, two failed due to temporary capacity fragmentation (insufficient contiguous GPU memory after allocation).
- Runtime errors: elevated NVTX kernel retries on quantized kernels for this model version — we saw more kernel fallbacks which increased per-token cost/time.

Short-term mitigations we can apply in next 30–60m (requires ops approval):
1) Evacuate low-priority workloads from the same cell (free ~18% headroom).
2) Temporarily route a portion of PrimeLedger traffic to a compatible hosted variant (slightly higher latency variability but reduces queueing).
3) Force a scale-up with looser packing constraints to avoid fragmentation (risk: higher overall GPU usage and cost).

Medium-term (post-incident):
- Increase reserved headroom for DL-2387 by +20% (billing/contract needed).
- Schedule a kernel/quantization review for the model variant — suspected regression in quantized kernel path.

I’ll keep watching. If we want to be conservative for the exec ask, recommend we present both a tactical 60m remediation and a commercial path (credit + headroom uplift) so PrimeLedger can decide.

-Marcus
